ai.title: Fix thinking block collapse state in CLI
ai.summary: Thinking blocks in the CLI now use stable `thinkingId` identifiers instead of index-based keys for collapse/expand state. `block-operations.ts` generates unique IDs via `generateThinkingId()`, and `ThinkingBlock` reads `thinkingId` from props rather than constructing it from `keyPrefix` and `startIndex`. `chat.tsx` updates collapse toggles to match by `thinkingId` directly. `thinking.tsx` simplifies the collapsed/expanded rendering logic by removing redundant left-border boxes and adjusting padding.

eli5.text: When you expand or collapse a thinking block in the CLI, it now remembers the right one even as the list changes. Previously the app tracked collapse state using the block's position in the list (its index), so expanding a block and then adding new blocks above it could collapse the wrong one or lose your place. Now each thinking block gets a stable, unique identifier generated when it is created, and the collapse/expand toggle matches blocks by that identifier instead of by position; the display logic was also simplified by removing redundant border elements and adjusting padding. You would notice this as more reliable expand/collapse behavior: clicking the toggle always affects the block you see it on, and the surrounding layout looks a bit cleaner. It is live today in the CLI.

ai.title: CLI build invokes SDK build directly
ai.summary: CLI binary build script now invokes `bun run --cwd ../sdk build` directly instead of calling the removed `build:sdk` wrapper script. This removes an indirection layer in the build pipeline. Changes affect `cli/package.json` and `cli/scripts/build-binary.ts`. The SDK build step remains a prerequisite for CLI compilation.

eli5.text: When you build the assistant's command-line tool, the build steps now talk directly to the SDK build process instead of going through an extra middleman step that has been removed. This affects only developers who compile the tool from source; if you just install and run the tool, you will not notice any difference. The underlying capability that gets built stays the same, it is just assembled in one fewer step.

ai.title: CLI button click fix
ai.summary: Updated `cli/src/components/button.tsx` to require both mouse down and mouse up events for click triggers. Added `useRef` to track mouse down state, preventing accidental clicks from hover events in some terminals. `handleMouseUp` fires `onClick` only if `mouseDownRef.current` is true, resetting on `handleMouseOut`.

eli5.text: When you click a button in the CLI using a mouse, it now waits until you both press down and release the mouse button before activating. Previously, just moving the mouse over the button could sometimes trigger a click by accident. You'd notice buttons no longer fire unintentionally from hover movements, giving you more precise control.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.562 release
ai.summary:
Bumps the Freebuff CLI release version to 1.0.562, bundling fixes from the surrounding same-day work: PostgreSQL transient-error retries with jittered backoff, isolated test-env helpers, the `ParamsOfUnion` type fix, and the CLI thinking-block collapse state using stable `thinkingId` keys.
The version bump itself touches only `cli/release/package.json` (1.0.561 -> 1.0.562), while the functional changes in this release span `packages/internal/src/db/transaction.ts`, `common/src/util/promise.ts`, `cli/src/types/function-params.ts`, `cli/src/components/block-operations.ts`, `cli/src/components/thinking.tsx`, and the CLI exit handler's renderer cleanup.
Notable for users: the 1.0.562 release includes the thinking-block collapse regression fix and the new TUI renderer cleanup before `process.exit(0)`, alongside behind-the-scenes PostgreSQL retries and test-environment hardening.
ai.evidence: Bump in `cli/release/package.json` changes `version` from `1.0.561` to `1.0.562`; no other code hunks in this commit.

eli5.text: This release makes the Freebuff assistant more reliable and polished, with better error handling when connecting to databases and smoother behavior when you close out of the terminal. Database transactions now retry automatically when there's a temporary connection problem, so you're less likely to see errors when the system is busy doing background work. The terminal screen now cleans up properly when you exit, preventing garbled output by resetting your terminal settings like mouse tracking and raw mode. Thinking blocks in the chat now remember their open or collapsed state correctly, so your view stays consistent as you scroll. Clicking buttons in the terminal interface is now more accurate, requiring both a press and release of the mouse button to trigger an action, which prevents accidental clicks from hover events. Additionally, updating dependencies and streamlining the build process means the software runs more smoothly and consistently in local development.

ai.title: Drop esbuild dep, transpile agents via Bun.build only
ai.summary: Removed esbuild from sdk/package.json dependencies. sdk/src/agents/load-agents.ts transpileAgent now relies solely on Bun.build, dropping esbuild dynamic import and fallback logic. web/next.config.mjs removes esbuild from serverExternalPackages.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to load a custom plugin or extra tool, it no longer relies on a helper library that was previously included alongside the core package. Instead, it uses a single built-in compiler tool whenever it needs to turn your plugin into something the system can run. You won't see any visible difference on your screen, but the way plugins are prepared behind the scenes is now simpler and depends on fewer moving parts. This change is live today and affects anyone using custom plugins or tools.
